title: Names for a pool schedule

blocks.text: A landscaping company schedules its jobs against a pool of identical crews with a cumulative constraint, so the plan says when each job starts and how many crews it needs, but not which crews. The foremen need names. Days are numbered from 0; a job that starts on day `s` and takes `d` days occupies days `s` to `s + d - 1`, and its crews are free again on day `s + d`.

Write `name_crews(jobs, crews)` in `handout.py`. `jobs` maps a job to `(start, days, need)` and `crews` lists the crew names. The plan respects the pool: on no day do the running jobs need more crews than `len(crews)`. Return a dict mapping each job to the list of crew names it gets, so that each job gets `need` distinct crews and no crew works on two jobs on the same day.
Use the hand-out rule: go through the jobs in order of start day, and give each job crews that are free on its start day. With $`f_c`$ the first day crew $`c`$ is free (0 at first):
Taking the free crews in name order makes the result easy to read, but any choice works. The tests check that the names keep every rule. About ten lines.

"""Run executes this file. Change the calls and see what prints. Submit grades."""
import logging

# Turn the logger up, so the `log.debug` lines of your code show under the printed lines.
logging.basicConfig(level=logging.DEBUG, format="%(levelname)s %(message)s")

from handout import name_crews

# Each job is (start_day, days, crews needed).
jobs = {"roof": (4, 2, 2), "fence": (0, 3, 1), "patio": (1, 2, 1), "shed": (3, 1, 1)}
named = name_crews(jobs, ["P", "Q", "R"])
for name in sorted(named, key=lambda n: jobs[n][0]):
    print(f"{name} {jobs[name]} gets crews:", named[name])

cases.says: jobs that never overlap can all go to one crew, and every job gets as many crews as it needs
every job gets a list of distinct crew names from the pool, as long as its need
jobs given in any order are handed out by start day, so the hand-out never runs short
a crew whose job ends at day e can start another job on day e, and not before
